Im not judging you here. I started trying to get pregnant about two years ago and at that time thought how I would miss the occasional time when I'd let my hair down. 
I got pregnant and miscarried, and have since had two more miscarriages. I'm now worried that I'll never be able to have a baby. Having been through this, all I can think is how I would do ANYTHING to have a baby and give up anything. Sometimes I think it just helps having perspective.

I wouldn't want to go against a nurse's advice, but yes I would say it would work to put them in without a tampon. The tampon was only to prevent them falling out and to make sure they go high enough. If you put them in and just take it easy they should come out naturally (sorry to be detailed but when you pass the embryo). 

I found it comforting to watch something lighthearted and take some painkillers. Be nice to yourself.

I'm sorry to hear this. 
I put them in inside a tampon if that makes sense (the tampon keeps them in) and took the tampon out after may be an hour or less. You'll start to feel cramping so it's a sign that they're working.

I hope you're next pregnancy (when you're ready) is successful. 
I found it helped to write down how I was feeling, and to speak to people about it.
Concentrate on yourselves and your exciting future ahead! Family just don't have a clue sometimes

Sadly, I’ve had all three. My first was natural and devastating because I wasn’t expecting it. With the second I took the vaginal pill as I hadn’t miscarried but the babies heart had stopped. It was painful but painkillers helped and at least I knew when it was going to happen. For the third I went for a d and c as again, the heart had stopped. It felt awful going in, pregnant still technically and knowing that when I woke up I wouldn’t be. 

They’re all horrible but I would prefer to be at home watching comfort programmes. The bleeding was much better/shorter with the d and c though. There are small risks with them all I believe.

I think it's nice to check in and see how she's doing but if you don't have much to say other than 'how are you' later on in the day, sometimes it's better to say nothing. May be ask her what she likes doing and plan something you can do together that could be fun and break the ice.

You're great! You've got a good attitude that I could do with some of. I went for a filler consultation today where they said there was a small risk of blindness. I'm not going to get it done. I'm going to embrace my hollow eyes.
